Music is the space lofi: the chord wash, the bells and plucks, the vinyl static. Ambience is the world's beds: the signal hum, crickets, the nest murmur, storm wind, dust. Effects are everything the colony does: footsteps, hammers, chimes, chirps, alerts. The lofi sits low by default so the colony reads over it — ride the faders however you like. Levels are yours for this visit; they reset when the page reloads.

COLONY LOG // THE COLONY REMEMBERS
Chronicle
INTERSTELLAR ANTS // $ANT COLONY BUILD v2.0 // ASSIGN THE CREW — SEND ANY ANT TO AN OPEN SCAFFOLD

Walk &
Think World

  • Procedural worlds from a seed — rolling violet hills, crystal fields, drifting spores, and landmarks placed by the roll of the dice, linked by glowing trails. Same seed, same world. Press R anywhere to roll a new one.
  • A living colony — worker ants haul, build, and forage on a day-and-night calendar, three structures rise scaffold by scaffold, and every ant remembers what you did.
  • Direct orders — walk up to any ant and press E: alongside the talk, every open scaffold that needs hands is listed right there — the founding builds, Rings commissions, and the works crew's current wilds project. Pick one and that ant walks straight to the scaffold, raises beams on the day shift, and speeds the build for every hand on site. Orders hold overnight, a finished scaffold releases its crew on its own, and an ant on recovery can't be ordered — rest comes first, per the Constitution.
  • A real sky — the stars above the colony are the brightest stars in Earth's actual sky, plotted true from an open star catalog, with constellation lines and the Milky Way behind them. At the Observatory, the Lens Keeper keeps a chart of the same sky — walk in and she unrolls it.
  • The night watch & the scout arm — when the day crew sleeps, the night watch takes the trails: two crews of five, one Shift Lead to four hands, ranked Night Tender, Night Warden, Shift Lead, and Night Captain over the whole watch. Scout parties of three, one Scout Lead to two, roam the wilds around the clock, ranked Scout, Pathfinder, Scout Lead, and Ranger. Talk to any of them; they know their place in the line.
  • The works crew builds the wilds out — lantern posts, supply depots, watchtowers, wells and gardens rise across the map, so no stretch of trail stays empty.
  • A census that breathes — the population grows hour by hour while storms, fevers, and hatchings push it back and forth. The Colony Log keeps score.
  • A constitution, not just a boss — the colony runs on written principles: shared responsibility, rest as a real state, and work that outlives its founder. Ants tire, recover, and cover for each other.
  • The Creative Lab — a warm workshop by a rose trail where tired ants go to make small things and come back steadier. What they build there stays standing, and the colony keeps count. After a storm its lamps stay lit late — and rested ants sometimes leave a dream piece on the quiet shelf, unexplained, exactly as it came to them.
  • Sky Harbor & aerial traffic — a landing pad station on its own teal trail, with beacon posts, a sky beam, and a harbor console. Supply pods fall to it, survey drones map the wilds, meteor showers and deep-sky freighters cross over — and the works crew pours smaller landing pads of its own out on the frontier.
  • The ladder past Lv5 — once the three founding structures stand, the colony takes commissions at the Rings Forge panel: an Ember Foundry that smelts foraged crystal into Glowglass, a Night Watchtower for the scout arm, the Resonance Spire, a Brood Atrium with winged messengers, and the Long Trail Gate, which opens a New Cycle with a legacy bonus.
  • The colony sounds alive — the Andromeda signal has a voice at the Observatory, ships call their approaches over Sky Harbor and kick up dust as they land and lift, and footsteps, hammer taps, lantern glass, ant voices, dawn birds, and night crickets all fade with distance, the way real sound does.
  • Save your colony to a file — the SAVE chip in the HUD downloads your whole colony: world seed, day, buildings, population, log, signal stage, and lab works. LOAD restores it anywhere. Keep the file; the page itself holds nothing between visits.
  • Colony Link — open this page in a second tab and that walker appears here as a live ghost ant.
  • No edge to the map — walk in any direction and new ground generates ahead of you, forever.
  • Slow space-lofi — a calm generative soundscape hums underneath it all once you enter.

WHAT'S NEW IN v2.0
  • Assign any ant to an open scaffold — get near an ant and press E. The conversation now carries the colony's open work: every rising scaffold that needs hands, with its build percentage, its distance, and how many ants are already assigned to it. That list is live — the three founding structures from the first morning, every Rings commission and the Satellite Station once commissioned, and whatever the works crew is currently raising out in the wilds. The neediest scaffold lists first.
  • Assigned ants actually go and build — an ant given an order leaves its post, walks to the scaffold, and works the beams there on the day shift (07:00–19:00), hammer-bob and all, exactly like a born builder. Every assigned hand standing at a scaffold speeds that build, on top of the crew's own pace — pile hands onto one scaffold to rush it, or spread them out. At night the order waits: the ant rests (or keeps watch, if it's watch crew) and picks the scaffold back up at 07:00. When the scaffold tops out, its assigned ants are released back to their posts automatically, and the Colony Log records every order given.
  • Orders respect the colony's rules — an ant on Constitution recovery shows in the conversation as ON RECOVERY and can't be ordered until it's back on post; storm shelter still pulls every ant off every scaffold; and any assigned ant can be released early with RETURN TO YOUR POST in the same conversation. The whole flow runs on the pad and the remote too — D-pad or stick to the order, A to give it, no keyboard needed. The HUD now counts open scaffolds and assigned hands live, and the Founder will tell you which scaffolds need hands if you ask him.
  • The star chart is holographic now — the Lens Keeper no longer unrolls paper. A holo-projector beside her telescope throws the same real catalog sky into the air as a slowly spinning globe of light, and walking into the Observatory calls up the full holographic chart: cyan projection glow, scanlines, and a light-sweep, with the stars themselves burning through the haze. Same 105 catalog stars, same true positions — just light now, not ink.
  • Conversations run on the controller — no more switching back to the keyboard mid-talk. With a conversation open, the D-pad or the left stick moves the highlight between replies and A picks the one you want; B leaves. The same pad navigation works in the Rings, Log, Sound, and Controller panels, the holographic star chart browses star to star on D-pad or stick, and a TV remote (or plain arrow keys + Enter) drives conversations exactly the same way.
  • A real sky — the stars overhead are no longer confetti. They are the 105 brightest stars in Earth's actual sky — Sirius, Betelgeuse, Vega, Antares, the Southern Cross — plotted at their true positions with their real magnitudes and colors, drawn from the open Yale Bright Star Catalog and baked into the page: no downloads, no external dependencies. Constellation lines join Orion, the Big Dipper, Cassiopeia, Cygnus, Scorpius and the Cross, and a faint Milky Way band runs behind them all. The same sky hangs over every seed; the colony just lives under it.
  • The Lens Keeper's star chart — walk into the Desert Lens Observatory and the Keeper unrolls her working chart: the same catalog sky as a star map. Click or tap any star for its name, constellation, magnitude, coordinates, and — for the famous ones — the Keeper's own notes. Simple exploring for now; she hints there is more astronomy folded into it for later.
  • The quiet shelf — ants who rest at the Creative Lab sometimes leave a dream piece behind: a small floating shape with a name like THE STAIR THAT RAINS UPWARD or THE GARDEN AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SKY. Nobody explains the dream pieces, nobody interprets them, and the Lab does not try. It just keeps them — they save with your colony, and Founder Anthony's ledger counts them like everything else the ants make.
  • After the storm, the Lab — when a spore storm passes, the Lab's lamps now stay lit late: the first worn ants to step off the line drift there to rest and make things, ahead of the nest ring. Recovery still runs on the Constitution's own rules — the storm just taught the colony where its tired ants want to be.
  • The Foundry loop, wired in the open — the colony's idea-to-world loop now runs as one small machine any system can pulse: CONVERSATION (talk an idea loose) → CONCEPT (plan it with your hands at the Lab) → CREATION (raise something, or finish a shared project) → OBSERVATION (look — the lens, the chart) → REFINEMENT (revisit a finished work). Every full turn is written into the Colony Log, the Rings ledger shows where the current idea stands, and the loop is the seam the Cognitive Foundry will plug into when it comes.
  • The audio is split — music, ambience, effects — the SOUND chip now opens a mixer: three buses under the master mute, each with its own toggle and fader. The space lofi (MUSIC) starts low at 32% so it sits under the colony; the world's beds (AMBIENCE: signal hum, crickets, nest murmur, storm wind, dust) ride at 70%; EFFECTS (footsteps, hammers, chimes, chirps, ship alerts) at 95%, clear over the music. Every proximity rule from v1.7 still applies per bus. The mix is yours for the visit and resets when the page reloads.
  • More lofi on the music bus — under the chord wash there is now a continuous gentle vinyl static bed with live crackle pops at irregular intervals, and sparse soft plucked notes wander in off a warm scale at random moments, like a lofi radio left on somewhere in the colony.
  • The shuttle stack — Sky Harbor's ships wear the colony's new colors: a white orbiter with a black underside and nose cap, riding a rust-orange external tank between two slim white boosters. The falling ship lands the same way it always did (E swings its bay door open for the manifest), the high freighter crosses in the same stack tipped into cruise, and Harbor traffic now flies half again as often — every approach, touchdown, and departure still calls its two-tone alert and kicks its dust.
  • Special project: the Satellite Station — once the Resonance Spire stands, the Rings panel offers a commission past the ladder (70 Dreams, 12 Glowglass): a dish array and control mound past the Observatory, raised over several days. When it stands, the shuttle stack launches the colony's first satellite from its pad. From then on the satellite crosses the sky every few minutes, blinking — during a pass the signal hum swells, scout reports come sharper and sooner, and pressing E at the station fires a scan pulse that lights the real crystal shards and spore blooms round the dish. Built, launched, and pass counts all save in the colony file, and the restore message reports them.
  • Five commissions past Lv5 — the Rings Forge panel now runs the colony's ladder. Lv6 Ember Foundry (30 Dreams, 30 crystals), Lv7 Night Watchtower (45 Dreams, 10 crystals, 6 Glowglass), Lv8 Resonance Spire (60 Dreams, 15 crystals, 10 Glowglass), Lv9 Brood Atrium (80 Dreams, 20 crystals, 14 Glowglass), Lv10 the Long Trail Gate (120 Dreams, 40 crystals, 20 Glowglass). Each unlocks only when the colony reaches its level, and each is crewed and raised on the day shift like every colony build.
  • Crystal in, Glowglass out — foragers have always hauled crystal shards home; now the colony banks them (watch the HUD). A finished Foundry smelts shards into Glowglass on work hours, and every build past Lv6 drinks Glowglass as part of its cost.
  • The signal speaks — stages 4 and 5 — with the Resonance Spire standing, the Lens Keeper's listening continues past the collective reading: the colony answers the long pause together, and then the pattern sends its first word. Stages unfold one per day, never repeat, and save with the colony.
  • The Watchtower works — while it stands, scout parties range far wider, file Colony Log reports more often, and young scouts earn Pathfinder stripes on duty.
  • Winged messengers — the Brood Atrium raises the population cap to 96 and hatches a flying caste: messengers cross the sky between sites hauling light freight, and every project in the colony builds half again as fast while they fly.
  • The Long Trail Gate & the New Cycle — a multi-day monument. When it stands, the colony celebrates at the gate, and Founder Anthony offers the New Cycle: a fresh world and a fresh ledger, carrying a legacy bonus (+40 starting Dreams and quicker building for every cycle completed).
  • Ship alerts & dust-off — Sky Harbor traffic now calls in: a two-tone landing alert sounds as pods, drones, and freighters approach or depart, loudest at the pad and fading with distance. Touchdowns and liftoffs kick up a burst of pad dust with a low rumble under it.
  • The signal has a sound — stand at the Observatory and the Andromeda signal hums under the static; each time a stage advances, its warbling transmission motif plays — louder up close, gone past the ridge.
  • A full proximity sound pass — footsteps change under your feet (nest earth, dirt, crystal fields), hammers tap at rising scaffolds, beams land with a wooden thock, lanterns chime in glass, every named ant greets you with its own chirp (the Founder's is deepest), scouts blow a soft horn when a report comes in, a dawn chorus opens the day shift, crickets take the night, the nest murmurs with the census, a finished Lab piece earns its jingle, and a spore storm raises the wind before it hushes the world. Every spatial sound is mixed by the distance between where it happens and your ant.
  • Save & load, reinforced — restoring a file now announces exactly what came back (day, seed, census, signal stage, structures, lab works, legacy), and SAVE keeps an in-session copy too: double-click LOAD to restore the colony you saved this session without hunting for the file.
  • The night watch — the colony no longer sleeps all at once. From 19:00 to dawn, Night Captain VESPER musters two night crews of five — one Shift Lead to four hands apiece — patrolling the landmark trails by lamplight while the day crew rests. Ranks run Night Tender, Night Warden, Shift Lead, Night Captain, and every promotion is just a harder stretch of trail done right.
  • Scout parties roam — two parties of three, one Scout Lead to two, range far past the lantern light on wide circuits of the wilds, day and night, breaking at the Nest between loops. Ranks run Scout, Pathfinder, Scout Lead, and Ranger TALON, who rides the widest circuit of all and answers for the whole scout arm.
  • The mark, top-left — the Space Ant logo now rides at the top left of this screen and stays with you in the corner of the HUD while you walk.
  • Random aerial events — the sky over the colony is busy now. Supply pods parachute down onto the Landing Pad (crack one open with E for its manifest and banked Dreams), a Harbor survey drone maps the wilds end to end, meteor showers streak overhead, and deep-sky freighters cross high and silent with their running lights on. Every pass is written into the Colony Log — and a spore storm closes the sky, cutting any flight short.
  • Landing pad stations — Sky Harbor stands on a new teal trail from the Nest: an octagonal pad with blinking beacon posts, a sky beam you can steer by, and a harbor console (press E) that reports sky traffic and the next drop window. The works crew has learned the pour, too — small landing pads now rise out in the wilds alongside its lanterns, depots, and wells.
  • The homepage wears the brand — this title screen now runs on the Space Ant colors straight off the mark: black, signal red, ember orange, and teal.
  • Save & resume, honestly — SAVE downloads a colony file (seed, day, construction, census, log, memories, signal stage, lab works, your position); LOAD reads it back and rebuilds that exact colony, and a damaged or wrong file is refused with a plain message instead of a broken world. Leaving is supposed to be easy: the colony waits in the file, not in a timer.
  • The Constitution, first layer — ants now carry a light stress ledger. Long work and storms wear them down; rest, night hours, and the Creative Lab bring them back. A worn-out ant steps off the line on its own and a rested one covers the work, so the colony no longer depends on any single ant, founder included. Ask Founder Anthony what holds the colony together.
  • The Creative Lab — follow the rose trail from the Nest: workbenches, planning screens, plants, a quiet alcove, and a shelf of miniatures the ants make together. Press E there to build on the shared project; finished pieces stay on display as the colony's creative legacy.
  • Spore storms — the frontier now pushes back. A warning comes first, then the colony shelters, work pauses, and a rising structure may lose a beam or two. Every storm is written into the Colony Log, and recovery runs through rest and the Lab.
  • The Andromeda signal advances — once the Relay stands, the Lens Keeper's reports now unfold over days: a faint pattern, then structured bursts, then the colony interpreting them together. Stages are remembered and saved; she will not repeat yesterday's news as if it were new.
  • Smoother ants, lighter phones — workers sidestep when they snag instead of grinding in place, keep polite spacing, and the phone HUD is trimmed down with a lower rendering load on touch devices.
  • Reliability pass (v1.3, kept) — the game checks itself at the door: if the engine or WebGL can't load, the title screen tells you why instead of leaving a dead button. Held keys clear when the window loses focus, and re-entering from pause no longer un-mutes your sound.
  • Colony Saddles — fitted at the Nest, never bought off a shelf: a Trail Lamp, a Signal Whip antenna, a Beam Cutter, and a Spore Tiller. Q swaps the tool, F works it. The crew wears saddles too, each fitted to its job.
  • Ant Senses — press X to see through the colony's own eyes: two compound lenses and three ocelli riding light and shadow at the top of your view.
  • Three camera views, raised higher — first person, third person, and the new Colony Eye overhead, all lifted for a more front-facing look. V cycles them.
  • Gamepad support — plug in an Xbox controller on PC and walk the colony with sticks and triggers. Full layout inside, on the Controller Map.
  • Roomier phone controls — smaller pads, spaced wider, with a LBL button that hides the labels once your thumbs know the way.

FIELD NOTE — A real ant sees through two compound eyes of 6 to 1,000 lenses apiece, plus three simple eyes called ocelli that read light and shadow. This colony is no different: the Ant Senses view (X) borrows exactly that kit, and the ocelli at the top of your screen brighten and dim with the sky.
